summary: Thomas Zehnder is an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang (1899–1977) worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, under John Dewey, and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Thubten Chodron (born 1950) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery. She held positions at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation, and founded Sravasti Abbey.

Thubten Jigme Norbu (1922–2008) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992) and as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. His students included Thubten Jigme Norbu, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Thubten Samphel (1956–2022) was a Tibetology scholar. He studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and Columbia University, and served at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thupten Jinpa (born 1958) is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Ganden Monastery, Zongkar Choede Monastery, and the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Ganden Monastery, Girton College, Stanford University, and the Institute of Tibetan Classics.
Thupten Tsering works in computational fields and Tibetology. He has held posts at Tibet University and the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

Théodore Pavie (1811–1896) was an Indology and Sinology scholar who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held the Sanskrit professorship at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

Thích Minh Châu (1918–2012) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He was a lecturer at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1961) and Vice Chancellor of Van Hanh University (~1964–1975).

Thích Nhất Hạnh (1926–2022) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Saigon, Columbia, and Princeton universities. He held academic posts at Columbia, Princeton, Van Hanh, and Cornell universities, and founded several Buddhist institutions.
Thích Thiện Châu (1931–1998) was a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued higher education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967–1971) and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1972–1977).

Tianshu Zhu specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed degrees at Northwest University and Ohio State University, the latter under John C. Huntington, and held positions at Shaanxi History Museum, Northwest University, Korea University, and Ohio State University.

Tilak Kariyawasam (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He later served as a professor at Leiden University from 1974 until ~2002.

Tim Dean (born 1964) is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of East Anglia, Brandeis University, and Johns Hopkins University. He held posts at Stanford University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the University of Washington, and the University at Buffalo.

Timothy H. Barrett (born 1949) is a Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge and Yale. He taught at the University of Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.
Timothy Lenz is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox at the University of Washington, where he later served as a faculty member and professor.
Timothy Lubin (born 1964) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University by 1994. He held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Mysore, Queen's College, Oxford, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari, later teaching at Maharaja's Sanskrit College (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1952).
